hypothesis: After the subscriber registry (PR #2914, squash 950c3f6cc) made delivery O(attached), the residual per-session event path at N=100 is: the registry lock + String hash + map probe + per-connection mpsc push + the wake + the per-connection serialize + the write syscall, 2 events per append. TASK: (1) baseline-decompose this residual at N=100/N=1 (CFS schedstat us/append, source-lane driver contract); (2) evaluate three behavior-preserving candidate classes — per-connection reserved serialization buffer (cand-a), registry lock granularity via per-session entry locks (cand-b), batch-drain coalescing of already-queued frames into one write (cand-c) — each gated by the wire oracle (6 session_event frames to attached, zero to unattached/late/post-detach) and D7 per-session FIFO; (3) paired ABBA per candidate at N=100 + N=1 controls, honest negatives valid.
approach: Parent-exact single-change branches off e6e7a26e4 (origin/rust at lane start; tip later moved 3x, ZERO overlap with this surface verified each move — supervisor.rs/subscribers.rs/clients.rs untouched upstream through ba4ea9d3b). sf-diag: a decomposition instrument (both relay publish sites stubbed; NOT a candidate, never ships; smoke-oracle-exempt by design) measuring the event-path TOTAL as base-minus-diag. cand-a: write_line_scratch (to_writer into a per-connection reserved Vec, byte-identical JSON, newline/write/flush pattern unchanged). cand-b: SessionSubscribers split into map lock (lookup only) + per-session entry locks (fan-out), attach holds the entry lock across its insert (delivery boundary == the TS .add() instant, same predicate as the single-lock registry), rebind holds BOTH entry locks in pointer order, register/move re-validate the entry against the map under the locks (stale-entry stranding race analyzed and closed), publish never drops empty entries (lifecycle owners only). cand-c: build_event_batch drains already-queued frames (<=32 frames / 256KiB, checked AFTER each serialized frame so nothing pulled is dropped) into one write; per-session FIFO is the queue's own recv order; nothing waits — first-frame latency unchanged; cross-class order vs ring events was already the select's nondeterministic interleaving (D6). Micro-bench (scratch crate, no product imports): component cost map at the N=100 shape. Driver: concurrent_io_curve.py (bench hillclimb sha 0cd875c7 = the source lane's VM copy, byte-verified) --workers {1,100} --appends 200 --seed-rows 20 --payload-size 2048; pa-daemon binaries (THE driver-contract binary — see the trap in validity), sha-asserted atomic swap per leg to /root/bin-cur, unique per-leg run paths, pre/mid/post calibration, dual-class I/O probe (40 isolated fresh+sync_all+rename @0.5s + 20 repeat-fsync) before EVERY leg with host-relative gates anchored from THIS host's best calm window (rep 0.7ms / fresh 1.15ms).
parity_notes: Wire oracle (smoke_registry.py, the source lane's script byte-identical) run TWICE per shipped binary on the VM: base + cand-a + cand-b + cand-c all PASS (6 session_event frames to the attached client over 3 appends; ZERO to an unattached connection, ZERO to a late attacher, ZERO post-detach; frame byte-shape parity after run-volatile normalization). D7 per-(session,connection) FIFO: preserved by construction in every candidate (one registry/entry lock per session orders all its publishers; the per-connection queue is FIFO; the batch drain is the queue's own order). cand-b keeps the exact single-lock delivery predicate (attach holds the entry lock across the insert) and the rebind both-or-neither atomicity (both entry locks, pointer order, no deadlock); the new stale-entry race is closed by map re-validation under the locks (a detached entry can only ever be empty). cand-c adds no new cross-class inversions (the select's arm order was already nondeterministic; TS's own cross-class order is timer-coalesced; one-syscall-per-batch is CLOSER to Node's Writable chunking than one-per-frame). Frozen surfaces untouched: session-JSONL bytes, compaction, RLM wire schemas, prompts, TUI bytes. Full reasoning: candidate-parity-notes.md in the evidence archive. sf-diag changes the client-visible event stream BY DESIGN (zero frames) and never ships; its legs validate on the session-file digest only (identical: 85607aee@N=100, 4195cad0@N=1 — matching the source lane's).

One measurement-arithmetic correction is disclosed in full: the first decomposition report divided the N=100 diag delta by N — wrong, the sup_cpu_per_append metric is already per-session-append; the N=1 diag battery caught it and the record states the corrected floor (~30-90us/session/append). The candidate-branch edit that produced cand-b's first binary was built from a diff missing one compile fix (or_insert_with(Arc::new)) — the binary was rebuilt from the verified diff and its smoke oracle re-passed before any cand-b leg; all binary shas in this record are the final, sha-asserted ones. The measurement-binary identity trap (pa-daemon vs the CLI) is a fleet-reusable lesson (the parent holds it for close-out refinement).
validity.honest_negative: NO candidate class clears its regime's noise band at either scale: the between-leg base spreads (54-192us/append across batteries) exceed every candidate's effect; the two regime-conditional observations (cand-c fast-fsync 1-leg pair -8.3%; cand-c N=1 append2 range separation) stay OBSERVATIONS — claiming them would be green-fishing. The task's premise (a residual wake floor worth attacking) resolves to a floor DOMINATED by receiver-side task-run overhead (~15-40us/wake), which none of the three classes removes: cand-a attacks a 0.1us term, cand-b a trigger the driver never produces, cand-c merges task-runs but the merge is only observable in regimes this host flips into mid-battery. A follow-up lane wanting this win needs a regime-controlled window (or a driver-side fsync-latency pin) and should start from the cand-c mechanism (task-run merge) — the only candidate whose observed deltas sit on the correct side in every clean pairing.
